sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Major discovery: the purple square is now at (50-52, 11-13), with center (51,12)! In other words, MOUSE(51,12) moved the purple square to (51,12)! My earlier check was wrong — the purple() function was matching the HUD's purple square at (4-6, 30-32), so it was reporting that the purple square hadn't moved. The actual purple square on the board moved from (55,8) to (51,12) — one step along the line!
So the mechanic is: MOUSE(row,col) on a dot moves the purple square to that dot. But the distance is… the purple square moved from (59,4) to (55,8) = 2 steps, then from (55,8) to (51,12) = 1 step. Hmm, so the purple square can move any distance? But the earlier MOUSE(31,32) (12 steps) didn't move it.
Wait, let me re-check the timeline:
- Step 3: MOUSE(31,32) — purple square at (59,4), no movement.
- Step 6: MOUSE(55,8) — purple square moved (59,4)→(55,8).
- Step 7: MOUSE(51,12) — purple square moved (55,8)→(51,12).
Hmm, so why didn't (31,32) work? Maybe the purple square can only move up to N steps per click, and N=2? (55,8) is 2 steps from (59,4) ✓. (51,12) is 1 step from (55,8) ✓. (31,32) is 12 steps from (59,4) ✗. This is consistent with max 2 steps per click!
Or maybe the purple square moves toward the clicked dot by up to 2 steps? If I had clicked (31,32), it should have moved 2 steps to (55,8). But it didn't move. So it's not "move toward the target" — it's "teleport to the clicked dot if within 2 steps."
Hmm, or maybe the max distance is measured in cells: (59,4)→(55,8) is Δ(4,4); (55,8)→(51,12) is Δ(4,4); (59,4)→(31,32) is Δ(28,28). Max Δ=4? That is, the purple square can jump up to 2 line-steps (4 cells) per click.
So the strategy: click dots 2 steps ahead repeatedly to move the purple square up the line toward the blue flower. The flower is at (11-17, 46-52), center (14,49). The dots on the line end at (19,44). The purple square needs to reach the flower — probably the final click is on the flower itself or the last dot.
But wait, what about the white "+" cursor? It disappeared after the first move. Maybe it was a "starter cursor" that was consumed. Or maybe it reappears. It's not important right now.
Also, what does ACTION7 (internal ACTION6) do? It also takes row/col. Maybe it's an "attack/click" action. Let's not worry about it for now.
Plan: move the purple square up the line in 2-step jumps: (47,16), (43,20), (39,24), (35,28), (31,32), (27,36), (23,40), (19,44), then to the flower (14,49)? The distance from (19,44) to the flower center (14,49) is Δ(5,5) — more than 4. Maybe the final move is a click on the flower. Or maybe the purple square needs to reach the last dot (19,44), and then a click on the flower completes the level.
Let me batch the clicks: (47,16), (43,20), (39,24), (35,28), (31,32), (27,36), (23,40), (19,44). After each click, verify the purple square's position and stop if it doesn't move. Then evaluate the final move.
Actually, to be safe, let's do them one at a time in a loop with verification, and stop if the purple square doesn't move as expected.

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def purple_board():
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='p' and n['pixels']==9:
            b=n['boundary']; rows=[p[0] for p in b]; cols=[p[1] for p in b]
            if min(rows)>8:  # exclude HUD
                return ((min(rows)+max(rows))//2, (min(cols)+max(cols))//2)
    return None
targets = [(47,16),(43,20),(39,24),(35,28),(31,32),(27,36),(23,40),(19,44)]
pos = purple_board()
print('start', pos)
for t in targets:
    action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':t[0],'col':t[1]}])
    new = purple_board()
    print('click', t, '->', new, 'moved:', new!=pos)
    if new==pos: break
    pos = new
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
